setting: A student checks out lab equipment with a lab supervisor before an afternoon chemistry practical.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a chemistry lab supervisor.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Excuse me. I'm in Professor Kim's afternoon lab, and I need to check out a digital balance and two graduated cylinders.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Sure. Are you on the lab roster for today? I'll need your student ID and the experiment number from the syllabus.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Here's my ID. It's experiment six—the titration lab. My partner is already saving a bench by the window.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Good. Balances can't leave the instrument room, so you'll weigh samples here and carry only the labeled vials back to your bench.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Got it. Do the cylinders have to be returned washed, or can we leave them in the rinse rack?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Rinse them at your sink, then place them on the drying rack by the window—not the dirty cart. We inventory everything before five.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: What if the balance reading jumps around? Last week mine wouldn't stabilize.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Close the draft doors, and wait for the green light. If it still drifts, move to balance three—balance two is out for calibration until Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Okay. Can I also get a pair of heat-resistant gloves for the hot plate?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes, but sign the glove log. Damaged gloves go in the red bin; don't put them back on the shelf.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Understood. Thanks—I'll bring the cylinders back before five.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.A: Checking out lab equipment and following lab rules
options.B: Changing the student's chemistry lecture section
options.C: Repairing a broken hot plate in the storeroom
options.D: Scheduling a make-up titration for next week

questions.explanation: She checks out a balance and cylinders and gets rules on use, return, and gloves.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing D because titration is named—that is today's experiment, not a make-up.

questions.narrator_text: Where must the student weigh her samples?

options.A: At her bench by the window

questions.explanation: Balances cannot leave the instrument room; she weighs there and carries labeled vials to the bench.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A because her partner saved a window bench—weighing stays in the instrument room.

questions.narrator_text: What should she do if balance two will not stabilize?

options.A: Use balance three because balance two is out for calibration
options.B: Shake the balance to reset it
options.D: Skip the weighing step until Thursday

questions.explanation: He says close the draft doors; if it still drifts, move to balance three—balance two is out for calibration until Thursday.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing D because Thursday is mentioned—that is when balance two returns, not when she skips work.

questions.narrator_text: What must the student do with heat-resistant gloves?

options.A: Buy a new pair at the bookstore first
options.B: Leave them on the dirty cart after use
options.C: Sign the glove log and put damaged gloves in the red bin
options.D: Share one pair with the whole lab section

questions.explanation: She may get gloves but must sign the glove log; damaged gloves go in the red bin, not back on the shelf.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing B because a rack/cart was mentioned for cylinders—gloves have a different rule.
